security_spec.violation_condition: The kernel uses CSRRS, CSRRC, CSRS, CSRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI (any read-modify-write CSR instruction) on a pmpaddr CSR, because the RMW cycle reads back the architectural 'reads as' value of bits like pmpaddr[G-1], not the underlying physical value, and writes that back — silently corrupting the underlying bit. This also applies to the kernel's csr_set(), csr_clear(), csr_read_set(), and csr_read_clear() macros when passed a pmpaddr CSR number.
security_spec.summary: pmpaddr[n][G-1] reads-as-0 but underlying value may be 1; CSRRS/CSRRC RMW will read 0, write it back, corrupting the underlying bit and silently weakening the PMP memory protection region

findings.finding: The kernel uses csrw (write-only CSR write) not CSRRS/CSRRC (RMW) to configure PMPADDR0. The value -1 is written directly to CSR_PMPADDR0, then PMPCFG0 is configured with NAPOT+RWX. The write-only csrw instruction does not read back the architectural 'reads as' value, so there is no risk of corrupting the underlying pmpaddr bits. An exception handler at .Lpmp_done safely handles the case where PMPs are not implemented.
findings.snippet:
li a0, -1
csrw CSR_PMPADDR0, a0
li a0, (PMP_A_NAPOT | PMP_R | PMP_W | PMP_X)
csrw CSR_PMPCFG0, a0

spec_citations.excerpt: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg.A[1] is set (NAPOT), then bits pmpaddr[G-2:0] read as all ones. When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg.A[1] is clear (OFF/TOR), then bits pmpaddr[G-1:0] read as all zeros. Although changing pmpcfg.A affects the value read from pmpaddr, it does not affect the underlying value stored in that register—in particular, pmpaddr[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.

findings.finding: The csr_set(), csr_clear(), csr_read_set(), and csr_read_clear() macros emit CSRRS/CSRC/CSRRS/CSRRC (RMW) instructions respectively. While these macros WOULD be dangerous if called with a pmpaddr CSR number, a comprehensive search of arch/riscv/ confirms no call site ever passes CSR_PMPADDR0 (or any computed pmpaddr CSR number) to any of these macros. All callers use safe CSRs: CSR_SSTATUS, CSR_ENVCFG, CSR_IP, CSR_HGEIE, CSR_HEDELEG, CSR_HENVCFG, CSR_HIE, CSR_HVIEN, CSR_VSIREG.

Only CSR_PMPADDR0 is defined (0x3b0). No CSR_PMPADDR1-63 definitions exist. The kernel has no dynamic PMP management code — it only configures PMP entry 0 once during early M-mode boot to allow all memory access. No post-boot PMP manipulation code exists in the kernel.
